question: Why might a user use Input Value parameters in OneStream?

options.A: To submit data directly to the cube.
options.B: To enter or change a value that will be used as an input.
options.C: To generate a flat list of values in a Cube View.
options.D: To hard-code a formatting value into a report.

explanation: B is correct: Input Value parameters allow a user to enter or change a value that will be used as an input. A is incorrect — submitting data to the cube is done through data entry forms. C is incorrect — a flat list of values is a Delimited List or Member List parameter. D is incorrect — hard-coding a formatting value is a Literal Value parameter.

question: What will be shown in a Cube View when defining a Delimited List parameter using single exclamation marks?

options.D: The member names from the metadata.

explanation: C is correct: when a Delimited List uses single exclamation marks, the Value Items are displayed in the Cube View — these are the actual metadata values passed to the filter. B is incorrect — Display Items appear when double exclamation marks are used; they provide friendly labels in place of metadata values. A is incorrect — the parameter name is an internal identifier. D is incorrect — raw metadata member names appear via Display Items configuration.

question: Which type of parameter requires more properties to be set compared to a Delimited List parameter?
explanation: D is correct: the Member List parameter requires more properties to be set than a Delimited List — it requires a Member Filter in addition to standard General properties. A is incorrect — Input Value has fewer configuration requirements. B is incorrect — Literal Value is the simplest type. C is incorrect — the specific comparison identified in the training is between Member List and Delimited List.

question: Which parameter type allows a user to enter or change a value directly in a field?
explanation: B is correct: an Input Value parameter allows direct entry or editing of a value in a field. A is incorrect — Delimited List provides a predefined list of selectable values. C is incorrect — Member List provides dimension members in a drop-down. D is incorrect — Bound List generates members via a method query or SQL.

question: Which two command types are available when creating a Bound List parameter in OneStream? (Select 2.)
explanation: A and B are correct: SQL and Method are the two valid command types for a Bound List parameter. C is incorrect — Tied is not a valid command type. D is incorrect — Descriptive is not a valid command type.

question: What is a benefit of using Literal Value parameters in OneStream?

options.A: Drop-down lists are easier to create.
options.B: Data is hard-coded into the report permanently.
options.C: VB.NET syntax is automatically converted to C#.

explanation: D is correct: Literal Value parameters centralize formatting values into a single parameter referenced by multiple components — when a change is needed, only the parameter needs updating. A is incorrect — drop-down lists use Delimited List, Member List, or Bound List. B is incorrect — hard-coding is not the primary benefit; centralization is. C is incorrect — Literal Value parameters do not convert syntax.

question: What is the primary difference between a Member Dialog parameter and a Member List parameter?

options.A: A Member Dialog parameter takes the user to a pop-up Select Member screen, while a Member List parameter shows a drop-down list.
options.B: A Member Dialog parameter provides a chat function with other users.
options.C: A Member Dialog parameter limits formatting functionality.
options.D: A Member Dialog parameter auto-selects the default member for the user.

explanation: A is correct: Member Dialog launches a pop-up Select Member dialog for hierarchy navigation, while Member List shows a flat drop-down list. B is incorrect — neither type provides a chat function. C is incorrect — Member Dialog does not limit formatting. D is incorrect — auto-selection is not the defining characteristic.

question: Why would the Display Items field be populated for a Delimited List parameter?

options.A: To ensure a user sees the member name used in the metadata.
options.B: To ensure a user sees a friendly member name instead of the metadata name.
options.C: To ensure a user can see the name of the parameter type being used.

explanation: B is correct: Display Items shows a friendly, readable label instead of the raw metadata name. A is incorrect — showing the metadata name is what happens WITHOUT Display Items; it is the opposite of the purpose. C is incorrect — Display Items shows member labels, not the parameter type name.

question: Which two command types are available with a Bound List parameter? (Select 2.)
explanation: A and B are correct: SQL and Method are the two valid command types. C is incorrect — Tied is not valid. D is incorrect — Descriptive is not valid.

question: What will a Member Dialog parameter provide access to?

options.B: An input field for typing a value.
options.D: A list of recently used members.

explanation: A is correct: Member Dialog provides a pop-up Select Member dialog box for hierarchy navigation. B is incorrect — an input field describes Input Value. C is incorrect — a drop-down list describes Member List or Delimited List. D is incorrect — recently used members is not a parameter type feature.

question: What is the purpose of specifying members in the Member Filter field for a Member List parameter?

options.A: To determine the members to include in the drop-down list.
options.B: To determine the members to exclude from the drop-down list.
options.C: To determine the friendly name displayed in the drop-down list.
options.D: To specify the default selected member.

explanation: A is correct: the Member Filter field defines which dimension members appear in the drop-down. B is incorrect — exclusions are handled by Remove expansions within the filter, not the field itself. C is incorrect — friendly names are managed through Display Items. D is incorrect — default selection is a separate setting.

question: How are Literal Value parameters typically used in a OneStream Cube View?

options.A: To correct spelling and grammar mistakes.
options.B: To allow a user to select members from a drop-down list.
options.C: To retrieve a data value from a cube.
options.D: To format Cube View columns, rows, and dashboard components.

explanation: D is correct: Literal Value parameters format Cube View columns, rows, and dashboard components by centralizing formatting values. A is incorrect — spelling corrections are made in text fields. B is incorrect — drop-down member selection uses Member List or Delimited List. C is incorrect — cube data retrieval uses GetDataCell or XFGetCell.

question: Which type of parameter uses a method query or complex expressions to retrieve members for a list?
explanation: C is correct: Bound List uses a method query or SQL expression to dynamically generate the list of members. A is incorrect — Delimited List uses manually defined values. B is incorrect — Member Dialog opens a Select Member pop-up. D is incorrect — Member List uses a Member Filter for a flat list of dimension members.

question: Which two database locations can be referenced in a Bound List parameter? (Select 2.)
explanation: A and B are correct: Bound List can reference the OneStream application database or an external database. C is incorrect — Microsoft Access is a specific product, not the correct category; 'external database' is the broader correct term. D is incorrect — Excel workbooks are not a Bound List data source.

question: What is one use case for Literal Value parameters in OneStream?

options.B: To standardize formatting in a Cube View.
options.C: To edit member names in the dimension.
options.D: To generate a drop-down menu for users.

explanation: B is correct: standardizing formatting across a Cube View by centralizing values into a parameter is a primary Literal Value use case. A is incorrect — durable data is set via isDurableCalculatedData. C is incorrect — member name editing is done in the Dimension Library. D is incorrect — drop-down menus use Delimited List, Member List, or Bound List.

question: Which tab in the Report Book designer is only active when a user has saved a book?
explanation: D is correct: the Preview tab is only active after a book has been saved, as rendering the output requires a saved file. A is incorrect — the Designer tab is active regardless of save status. B is incorrect — the Report tab is available before saving. C is incorrect — the Book tab is available before saving.

question: From which two locations can report books be opened in OneStream? (Select 2.)
explanation: B and D are correct: report books can be opened from the XF file system (within the OneStream application) and from the Local folder on the user's machine. A is incorrect — Cube View Profiles manage Cube View Group access, not report book locations. C is incorrect — Workflow is for data collection processes.

question: Which report book file type is an Excel-based book where reports appear on separate tabs with no preview available in the Book Designer?
explanation: B is correct: xfDoc.xlBook is the Excel-based book type — reports appear on separate tabs and no preview is available in the Book Designer. A is incorrect — xfDoc.pdfBook is the PDF type and is the default; preview is available with the correct suffix. C is incorrect — xfDoc.zipBook compresses books into a single file. D is incorrect — xfDoc.htmlBook is not a standard file type.

question: Which suffix must be included in every report book filename in OneStream?
explanation: B is correct: all report book filenames must include xfdoc (e.g., ReportBookName.xfDoc.pdfBook). A is incorrect — doc is a Word extension. C is incorrect — xffile is not valid. D is incorrect — xfbook is not valid.

question: Which two options can report books consist of in OneStream? (Select 2.)
explanation: B and D are correct: report books can include Cube Views and Extensible documents. A is incorrect — Time profiles are for workflow period definitions. C is incorrect — journal templates are for data collection.

question: Which suffix must be used in a report book filename in OneStream?
explanation: B is correct: xfdoc is the required suffix in every report book filename. A is incorrect — doc is a Word extension. C is incorrect — xffile is not valid. D is incorrect — xfbook is not valid.

question: From which two locations can report books be opened in OneStream? (Select 2.)
explanation: A and C are correct: report books can be opened from the XF file system and from the Local folder. B is incorrect — Cube View Profiles manage Cube View Group access. D is incorrect — Workflow is for data collection processes.

question: Where are report books edited in OneStream?
explanation: D is correct: report books are edited in the Designer tab of the Book Designer. A is incorrect — the Preview tab shows rendered output of a saved book. B is incorrect — Application tab is not the editing interface. C is incorrect — Reports tab is not the editing interface.

question: Which two report book file types confirm the report output format in OneStream? (Select 2.)
explanation: A and C are correct: xlBook produces Excel output and pdfBook produces PDF output — both are valid file type suffixes. B is incorrect — pngBook is not a valid type. D is incorrect — vttBook is not a valid type.

question: Which tool is used to create or amend report books in OneStream?
explanation: C is correct: the Book Designer is the tool for creating and amending report books. A is incorrect — Books Dashboard is not a standard tool name. B is incorrect — Books Application is not a standard tool. D is incorrect — Report Builder is not a OneStream term for this.

question: Which two actions can a user take when using the Report Book toolbar? (Select 2.)

options.A: Access the Report Book Task Activity.
options.C: Move a book item one level into an existing hierarchy.

explanation: A and C are correct: the toolbar allows accessing Report Book Task Activity and moving a book item one level into an existing hierarchy. B is incorrect — organizing into categories is not a toolbar action. D is incorrect — closing a book is a standard file operation, not specifically a toolbar action.

question: Which tab in the Report Book designer is only active when a user has saved a book?
explanation: C is correct: the Preview tab becomes active only after a book has been saved. A is incorrect — Designer tab is available before saving. B is incorrect — Report tab is available before saving. D is incorrect — Book tab is available before saving.

question: What do report books do in OneStream?

options.A: They render reports faster than any other OneStream reporting solution.
options.B: They allow users to combine a variety of reports and files into one document.
options.C: They are used to query cube data and present it to the user.
options.D: They specify the kind of data used within a dashboard.

explanation: B is correct: report books allow users to combine a variety of reports and files into a single output document. A is incorrect — rendering speed is not the defining purpose. C is incorrect — querying cube data describes Cube Views. D is incorrect — specifying dashboard data types is a dashboard function.

question: Which report type is supported when adding a report to a report book in OneStream?
explanation: D is correct: a Dashboard chart is a supported report type for report books. A is incorrect — Forms are data entry tools. B is incorrect — Spreadsheet is not specifically identified here as a report type. C is incorrect — Pivot Grid is not a supported type.

question: Why are loops used in report books in OneStream?

options.A: They customize how many times a book is printed.
options.B: They provide the capability to customize what data needs to be viewed.
options.C: They customize graphics used in books.
options.D: They customize the recipient list when books are run.

explanation: B is correct: loops customize what data needs to be viewed — for example, iterating through entities to produce separate report sections. A is incorrect — print count is not the purpose. C is incorrect — graphics customization is a formatting concern. D is incorrect — recipient lists are handled through distribution settings.

question: Which two items are valid Change parameters in OneStream report books? (Select 2.)
explanation: C and D are correct: Workflow and POV are the valid Change parameters that update context as a book loops. A is incorrect — Channels is not a valid Change parameter. B is incorrect — Overrides is not a valid Change parameter.

question: Why are If statements used in report books?

options.A: They determine how book items within the statement hierarchy are processed.
options.B: They eliminate the use of parameters in a book.
options.C: They improve the speed of data retrieval within a book.
options.D: They determine where books are saved once run.

explanation: A is correct: If statements add conditional logic determining how book items are processed. B is incorrect — If statements and parameters serve different purposes. C is incorrect — If statements add logic, not retrieval speed. D is incorrect — save location is a configuration setting.

question: Which two items are valid Change parameters in OneStream report books? (Select 2.)
explanation: C and D are correct: Workflow and POV are the valid Change parameters. A is incorrect — Channels is not valid. B is incorrect — Overrides is not valid.

question: What should a user add to an XLBook in OneStream?
explanation: C is correct: File items are added to an XLBook, appearing as separate tabs within the Excel workbook. A is incorrect — PDF items belong to pdfBook. B is incorrect — 'Report components' is too vague. D is incorrect — Dashboard widgets are dashboard elements.

question: Which report type is supported when adding a report to a report book in OneStream?
explanation: B is correct: Dashboard chart is the supported report type. A is incorrect — Forms are data entry tools. C is incorrect — Spreadsheet is not specifically identified here. D is incorrect — Pivot grid is not supported.

question: Why are loops used in report books in OneStream?

options.A: They customize how many times a book is printed.
options.B: They provide the capability to customize what data needs to be viewed.
options.C: They customize graphics used in books.
options.D: They customize the recipient list when books are run.

explanation: B is correct: loops customize what data is viewed by iterating through content. A is incorrect — print count is not the purpose. C is incorrect — graphics is a formatting concern. D is incorrect — recipient lists use distribution settings.

question: What should be created before attempting to use an Else or Else If statement in a report book?
explanation: C is correct: an If statement must exist before Else or Else If can be used — they are continuations of an existing conditional block. A is incorrect — a Cube View is a reporting object, not a prerequisite. B is incorrect — a Member Filter is a Cube View element. D is incorrect — a description is optional metadata.

question: Why are If statements used in report books?

options.A: They determine how book items within the statement hierarchy are processed.
options.B: They eliminate the use of parameters in a book.
options.C: They improve the speed of data retrieval within a book.
options.D: They determine where books are saved once a Data Management Sequence is run.

explanation: A is correct: If statements determine how book items are processed with conditional logic. B is incorrect — parameters and If statements serve different purposes. C is incorrect — If statements add logic, not speed. D is incorrect — save location is a configuration setting.

subtopic: Quick Views — Edit Quick View Options
question: What are Edit Quick View Options used for in the OneStream Spreadsheet Add-In?

options.A: To apply default behaviors, display settings, and suppression settings for all items in an open spreadsheet.
options.B: To apply calculations within a spreadsheet.
options.C: To apply behaviors, display settings, and suppression settings for a selected Quick View.
options.D: To convert a Quick View to formula-based cell retrieves.

explanation: C is correct: Edit Quick View Options applies settings to the selected Quick View specifically. A is incorrect — applying to all items describes Quick View Preferences. B is incorrect — calculations use Excel formulas or OneStream functions. D is incorrect — converting to formula-based retrieves uses Convert to XFGetCells.

question: What are Quick View Preferences used for in the OneStream Spreadsheet Add-In?

options.A: To apply default behaviors, display settings, and suppression settings for all items in an open spreadsheet.
options.B: To apply calculations within a spreadsheet.
options.C: To apply behaviors, display settings, and suppression settings for a selected Quick View.
options.D: To configure Cube View Connection settings.

explanation: A is correct: Quick View Preferences applies default settings globally to all items in an open spreadsheet. B is incorrect — calculations use Excel or OneStream functions. C is incorrect — per-Quick-View settings use Edit Quick View Options. D is incorrect — Cube View Connections are configured separately.

question: Where can Default Expansions for row and column settings be found within the OneStream Spreadsheet Add-In?

options.D: Data tab of the Quick View

explanation: C is correct: Default Expansions are found under Preferences, controlling how rows and columns expand when double-clicked. A is incorrect — Edit Quick View Options applies per-Quick-View settings but not Default Expansions. B is incorrect — the Home Ribbon provides general options. D is incorrect — the Data tab does not contain Default Expansion settings.

question: What does the Convert to XFGetCells option allow users to do in the OneStream Spreadsheet Add-In?

options.A: Convert dimension members from an existing Quick View to a new Quick View.
options.B: Convert to formula-based retrieves on intersections of data within an existing Quick View.
options.C: Convert to data adapters within a refined dashboard.
options.D: Convert formatted cells to static data intersections.

explanation: B is correct: Convert to XFGetCells converts an existing Quick View's data intersections into formula-based retrieves that persist as cell-level formulas. A is incorrect — converting members to a new Quick View is not this option's function. C is incorrect — data adapters are dashboard components. D is incorrect — converting to static data removes live connection; XFGetCells maintains formula-based connection.

subtopic: Quick Views — Edit Quick View Options
question: Where are the Edit Quick View Options found within the OneStream Spreadsheet Add-In?

options.B: By right-clicking on a selected Quick View.

explanation: C is correct: Edit Quick View Options is found within the Quick View toolbar. A is incorrect — the Home ribbon has general options but not Edit Quick View Options specifically. B is incorrect — right-clicking provides a context menu, but Edit Quick View Options is in the toolbar. D is incorrect — Preferences contains global default settings.

question: What happens to standard formatting applied within a Quick View when the sheet or workbook is refreshed?

options.A: The user will be prompted to save the formatting.
options.B: The formatting will still be retained.
options.C: The formatted cells will revert to what was applied prior to the standard formatting.
options.D: The formatted cells will be permanently deleted.

explanation: C is correct: standard formatting reverts to what was applied before the standard formatting was added — the formatting is lost on refresh. A is incorrect — no prompt is given; formatting simply disappears. B is incorrect — standard formatting is NOT retained after refresh. D is incorrect — the cells themselves are not deleted; only the standard formatting is lost.

question: A user wants to add Operating Expenses to rows containing members from the same account hierarchy in a Quick View. What is the correct member definition syntax?
explanation: C is correct: when adding a member from the same existing hierarchy, neither the A# token nor the # symbol is needed — just the member name (OpEx). A is incorrect — the A# dimension token is not required for members within the same hierarchy. B is incorrect — the # symbol is also not needed. D is incorrect — Account#OpEx is not valid OneStream syntax.

subtopic: Quick Views — Edit Quick View Options
question: Where are the Edit Quick View Options found within the OneStream Spreadsheet Add-In?
explanation: C is correct: Edit Quick View Options is in the Quick View toolbar. A is incorrect — Preferences has global default settings. B is incorrect — Home ribbon has general options. D is incorrect — Settings is not the location.

question: What does the Quick View POV display in the OneStream Spreadsheet Add-In?

options.A: The default POV settings used within a Cube View Connection.
options.B: The default POV settings excluded from a Quick View.
options.C: The default POV used when a dimension member is not present in the rows or columns.
options.D: The default POV used when a Cube View is not visible.

explanation: C is correct: the Quick View POV shows the default member for dimensions not explicitly represented in the rows or columns. A is incorrect — Cube View Connection settings are separate. B is incorrect — the POV does not show excluded settings. D is incorrect — it is not related to Cube View visibility.

subtopic: Quick Views — Edit Quick View Options
question: What are Edit Quick View Options used for in the OneStream Spreadsheet Add-In?

options.A: To apply default behaviors and settings for all items in an open spreadsheet.
options.B: To apply calculations within a spreadsheet.
options.C: To apply behaviors, display settings, and suppression settings for a selected Quick View.
options.D: To configure Cube View Connection settings.

explanation: C is correct: Edit Quick View Options applies settings to the selected Quick View specifically. A is incorrect — applying to all items describes Quick View Preferences. B is incorrect — calculations use Excel or OneStream functions. D is incorrect — Cube View Connections are configured separately.

question: What happens to standard formatting applied within a Quick View when the sheet or workbook is refreshed?

options.A: The user will be prompted to save the formatting.
options.B: The formatting will still be retained.
options.C: The formatted cells will revert to prior formatting.
options.D: The formatted cells will be lost within the Quick View.

explanation: D is correct: standard formatting is lost when a Quick View is refreshed — it does not persist. A is incorrect — no prompt is given. B is incorrect — standard formatting is not retained. C is incorrect — while the cells revert in appearance, 'lost' more precisely captures the outcome in this context.

question: Where can users apply Excel Styles to a selected Quick View in the OneStream Spreadsheet Add-In?

options.B: Quick View Toolbar > Edit Quick View Options

explanation: B is correct: Excel Styles are applied to a selected Quick View via Quick View Toolbar > Edit Quick View Options. A is incorrect — Preferences applies global settings. C is incorrect — that path is not the location for Excel Styles. D is incorrect — Quick View Toolbar > Preferences does not exist as a specific path.
